title: The Principle of Cognitive Dissonance
text:
Cognitive dissonance theory describes the mental discomfort experienced by a person who simultaneously holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values. This state of psychological tension is powerful because it drives an intrinsic motivation to achieve consonance and reduce the perceived inconsistency within one's belief structure.

The magnitude of this dissonance is proportional to the importance of the cognitions involved. To resolve the discomfort, individuals often employ several strategies: changing one of the dissonant behaviors, altering a conflicting attitude, or adding new consonant beliefs that rationalize the contradiction. This process frequently leads to self-persuasion and selective exposure to information.
